segments.t: What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH007Coding agentsKTPH008 — korTTY recognises Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI in local shell tabs and classifies each pane as working, blocked on a question, done or idle, and now shows it everywhere: a glyph in the tab title, chips, accent bars, rollups and pane rows in the dashboard (which expands to a waiting agent and offers Send Enter / Esc / Interrupt in the context menu), a dockable KTPH009Coding AgentsKTPH010 panel (KTPH011View → Coding AgentsKTPH012, KTPH013KTPH001KTPH014+KTPH015KTPH002KTPH016+KTPH017KTPH003KTPH018) listing every agent of every window with one-click answers (y, n, Enter, Esc, ↑, ↓, Ctrl+C), Explain, Rename and a prompt box, a status-bar strip, KTPH019KTPH004KTPH020+KTPH021KTPH005KTPH022+KTPH023KTPH006KTPH024 to jump to the next waiting agent, a badge with the number of waiting agents on the app icon (Dock, Windows taskbar, KDE/Ubuntu launcher; window title elsewhere) and a desktop notification when an agent needs a decision or finishes while you are not looking at its pane. Detection reads the terminal screen locally and can be switched off in KTPH025Settings → Terminal → Coding agentsKTPH026, where the badge and the notifications have their own toggles; the rules are JSON files you can override under KTPH000. See KTPH027Coding agentsKTPH028.

KTPH004Control API and KTPH000KTPH005 — korTTY can now open a local socket so a script or a coding agent on the same computer can list your windows, read any pane, type into it, wait for output, split a local shell, and drive a detected coding agent. It is KTPH006off by defaultKTPH007 and is switched on under KTPH008Settings → Terminal → Control APIKTPH009, where a status line reports what the listener is actually doing. Nothing is reachable over the network and no other user of the computer can connect: the endpoint lives in an owner-only KTPH001 directory and needs a token that is regenerated on every start. Every action is logged with byte counts only, never terminal text, and the first time a program types into a pane you get one desktop notification, so a takeover is never silent. An administrator can deny the feature outright with the KTPH002 policy key. The KTPH003 client ships beside the application in every native package and handles discovery, authentication and exit codes for you. See KTPH010Control APIKTPH011 and KTPH012Control CLIKTPH013.

KTPH000Anonymous usage statistics now cover coding agents and the Control APIKTPH001 — if you allowed anonymous statistics, korTTY also reports which agent kinds are detected, how often agent notifications fire, which Control API methods are used and whether the coding-agent and Control API settings are on. Only kinds, states, method names and counts are sent — never terminal text, prompts or pane names. See KTPH002Anonymous dataKTPH003.

KTPH009Ctrl+L and Ctrl+F reach the shell on Windows and LinuxKTPH010 — the terminal's own Clear Buffer and Find took these keys, so KTPH011KTPH001KTPH012+KTPH013KTPH002KTPH014 wiped the scrollback instead of redrawing the screen in bash, psql or a REPL, and KTPH015KTPH003KTPH016+KTPH017KTPH004KTPH018 never moved the cursor forward or paged forward in KTPH000. Both keys now go to the shell; Clear Buffer and Find stay in the terminal's right-click menu and Find in KTPH019Edit → Find…KTPH020, while KTPH021KTPH005KTPH022+KTPH023KTPH006KTPH024 and KTPH025KTPH007KTPH026+KTPH027KTPH008KTPH028 on macOS are unchanged. On Linux a selection copied automatically also becomes the X11 primary selection, so a middle-click pastes it in other applications. See KTPH029Keyboard shortcutsKTPH030.

KTPH000The ANSI colors and the selection color on the Colors tab now take effectKTPH001 — the 16 color pickers in KTPH002Settings → ColorsKTPH003 were never saved, and the terminal ignored the KTPH004SelectionKTPH005 color too. Both now apply to every open terminal as soon as you save, and terminal recordings use the same colors as the screen. Settings you never changed keep the built-in palette and inverse-video selection, so nothing looks different until you customize a color. KTPH006Bold as bright colorKTPH007 still affects recordings only. See KTPH008ColorsKTPH009.

KTPH001Review and replace a changed host keyKTPH002 — when a server was rebuilt, the changed-key alert of a terminal tab or the SFTP manager now offers KTPH003Review and Replace…KTPH004: it shows the trusted and the new SHA-256 fingerprint side by side and replaces the key only after you tick that you verified the new fingerprint with the server administrator. KTPH005CloseKTPH006 and KTPH007CancelKTPH008 stay the default buttons, background connections never offer the replacement, and the KTPH000 policy forbids it. The new KTPH009Configuration → Security → Known Hosts…KTPH010 lists, searches and removes trusted keys. See KTPH011SSH host-key verificationKTPH012.

KTPH000Temporary SSH keys are no longer left in the temp folderKTPH001 — every connect, split and SFTP session with a temporary SSH key wrote the private key to a file in the system temp folder that was never deleted, so the key stayed on disk long after it had expired, and the debug log recorded the beginning and end of the key text. Temporary keys are now read in memory only and never logged, and key files that earlier versions left behind are deleted at the next start when they belong to you. See KTPH002SecurityKTPH003.

KTPH001Scheduled jobs keep temporary keys off the disk tooKTPH002 — a JobScheduler job with a temporary SSH key now authenticates in memory like a terminal tab. Only an Rsync job still needs the key as a file for its external KTPH000; that file is created owner-only from the start and deleted when the job ends or its connection fails, instead of staying in the temp folder.

KTPH000Go back to an older llama.cpp or MLX runtimeKTPH001 — when a new runtime release causes problems, KTPH002Other version…KTPH003 in the Runtimes table of KTPH004AI → AI Manager → Local ModelsKTPH005 lists every version the signed stable channel still offers for this computer and installs the one you choose through the same verification as an update. A version other than the newest stays KTPH006pinnedKTPH007, so update checks keep it until you pick the newest version again or choose KTPH008UnpinKTPH009; a pinned version the channel later withdraws is dropped automatically. See KTPH010RuntimesKTPH011.

KTPH000Both runtimes stay visible in the Runtimes tableKTPH001 — the table had a fixed height that fit two rows only at the default font, so with a larger UI font scale or an AtlantaFX design only llama.cpp was visible and MLX needed scrolling. The table now sizes itself to its rows and follows font-scale and design changes while the AI Manager is open.

KTPH000Being offline is no longer reported as a failed runtime updateKTPH001 — the startup check for the llama.cpp and MLX runtimes ran into an error with a stack trace whenever the computer had no network yet. An unreachable channel now ends in an KTPH002OfflineKTPH003 status and a single log line, installed runtimes stay usable, and an installation you start yourself still says why it did not happen.

KTPH000MLX runtime updates are published like llama.cpp onesKTPH001 — the MLX index is now read from the same immutable, versioned releases as the llama.cpp index instead of a release whose files were replaced on every update; builds fall back to the previous location until the first combined release exists.

KTPH000Attach the selected file to an AI requestKTPH001 — when the text you right-click in the terminal is a single file name, KTPH002AI → Summarize / Solve Problem / AskKTPH003 and KTPH004Ask Agent…KTPH005 offer to send that file's content along with the request, so the model can work with the file rather than only its name. The file is resolved against the pane's current directory (over SFTP in SSH tabs, from disk in local-shell tabs) and is attached only after korTTY has checked that it exists, is readable, is UTF-8 text and fits the profile's selection limit; a checkbox in the confirmation dialog lets you send the text alone. The attachment is shown above the chat, stays in context for follow-up prompts and is kept with a saved chat. A KTPH006FlowchartKTPH007 button beside it renders a Mermaid flowchart of the attached script in the chat. See KTPH008Attaching a selected file to the chatKTPH009.

KTPH004The AI agent asks before it runs in a switched sessionKTPH005 — after KTPH000, KTPH001 or a nested KTPH002 in a terminal, the agent's commands would still run over the tab's original connection, as the user the tab was opened with, not as the user the prompt shows. AI Agent and AI Planning now warn first and name the KTPH003 (or "on this computer" in a local-shell tab) the commands will really run as; KTPH006CancelKTPH007 is the default. The check also covers rerunning a command with the activity panel's reload button and the execution of an accepted plan. See KTPH008Safety and failure handlingKTPH009.

KTPH000No internet mode for native Anthropic profilesKTPH001 — korTTY sends no web tools to the native Anthropic Messages API, so a mode such as KorTTY Tavily Tool had no effect there. For such profiles the KTPH002Internet accessKTPH003 dropdown is now locked to KTPH004DisabledKTPH005 with a hint explaining why. See KTPH006AI internet accessKTPH007.

KTPH000See what AI costsKTPH001 — an AI profile can now carry a price per one million input and output tokens (KTPH002AI → AI Manager → ProfilesKTPH003, KTPH004Price per 1M tokensKTPH005). With a price, korTTY shows the money spent next to the quota bar ("≈ 3.42 € in this period"), on session journals and in the AI Swarm header; local models are marked as having no token costs. See KTPH006Token quota managementKTPH007.

KTPH000Session journals show their AI tokensKTPH001 — every AI call made for a journal (summaries, title, screenshot analysis, questions) is added to the journal: the journal page header shows the total and the journal manager has an KTPH002AI tokensKTPH003 column with a breakdown in its tooltip. See KTPH004AI token usage and costKTPH005.

KTPH000All AI calls count towards the profile quotaKTPH001 — session journal calls, every AI Swarm agent and the swarm's combined answer, and scheduled AI jobs were not added to the profile's token quota before; they now are, so the quota bar reflects what was really spent. The AI Swarm header also shows the total tokens of the whole run.

KTPH001Scheduled AI agent jobs no longer hide a number in their outputKTPH002 — the job's token count was treated like a secret, so every occurrence of that number in the job's output and journal was replaced by KTPH000. It is now booked against the profile quota instead.

KTPH000Session journal per runKTPH001 — a job can now record a full session journal for every run: one journal per target server with every command, its output, the job's summary and the outcome, which can be summarized by the AI, searched, exported and asked questions like an interactive journal. Per job you choose when the AI summarizes (every kept run, only failed runs, or never), whether successful runs are kept at all, when the journals are deleted automatically (after N days, on a date, or never), a maximum number of runs and disk space, whether a run identical to the previous one is discarded in favour of a reference, and which AI profile summarizes — a local profile keeps it free. Switching the journal or its AI summaries on first shows a warning with an estimate of the tokens and cost per run, day and month. The run history shows each run's journals with tokens and cost and opens them in the viewer; scheduled AI Swarm jobs record one journal per server as well. Administrators can forbid automation journals or cap their retention, disk space and number of runs. See KTPH002Session journal per runKTPH003.

KTPH001Screenshots of jobs from an invisible virtual terminalKTPH002 — COMMAND and snippet jobs with a session journal can run in a pseudo terminal that korTTY renders without any window: screenshots at an interval, when the screen changes and at the end land in the run's journal, and a runtime limit stops monitors such as KTPH000 with Ctrl+C. Progress bars and AI coding tools in non-interactive mode become visible without disturbing the terminals you are working in. See KTPH003Virtual terminal and screenshotsKTPH004.

KTPH000Session journal per swarm runKTPH001 — the KTPH002Session journalKTPH003 checkbox in the AI Swarm toolbar records one journal per server for every run: the agent's commands and output, its answer and the combined report, with the same settings as a job (⚙) and the same cost warning. The dashboard reports what was kept and what the journal summaries cost, and KTPH004OpenKTPH005 shows the journals. See KTPH006Session journal per runKTPH007.

KTPH000Journals grouped by job and swarm, with badgesKTPH001 — the journal manager now groups automation journals by their job or swarm and by run, with the totals of each group, a filter for interactive, JobScheduler, AI Swarm, failed or pinned journals, and badges for the source, outcome, AI mode, identical runs, pin and the time left until automatic deletion. See KTPH002Managing journalsKTPH003.

KTPH000Temporary SSH keys are no longer sent to the AI with a multi-server workflowKTPH001 — KTPH002Generate multi-server workflowKTPH003 sent the complete private key of a temporary SSH key to the AI provider. The request now only states that the server uses a temporary key. The path of a key file is still sent, so the script can use it. See KTPH004Generate multi-server workflowKTPH005.

KTPH000Unlock the vault after startupKTPH001 — with KTPH002Require master password on startupKTPH003 turned off, korTTY started with the vault locked and offered no way to enter the master password later. KTPH004Configuration → Security → Unlock Vault…KTPH005 now opens the vault mid-session, and the "vault locked" messages for saving keys and passwords, AI Swarm, guide questions and workflow scripts have an KTPH006Unlock Vault…KTPH007 button that continues the action once the vault is open. Temporary SSH keys that a locked start could not decrypt are restored on unlock instead of being lost on the next save. See KTPH008Unlocking the vault laterKTPH009.

KTPH000Dialogs open noticeably fasterKTPH001 — the WebKit engine is loaded in the background after start instead of on the first dialog that needs it, the AI Manager and the settings dialog build their tabs on first visit, a stored connection's secrets are no longer re-derived on every open, and the snippet editor keeps a ready editor in reserve. Measured on a development build, the first AI Manager open dropped from about 1.4 s to under 0.1 s and the settings dialog from about 350 ms to 45 ms. The spare editor can be switched off with KTPH002Keep a pre-warmed editor readyKTPH003. See KTPH004Snippet Editor settingsKTPH005.

KTPH000The built-in guide has a new look and a working offline searchKTPH001 — the guide now uses the Dracula theme, because the previous theme reaches end of life in November 2026. Search works without a network connection and suggests results as you type, and German pages now declare German as their language, so screen readers and hyphenation use the right one.

KTPH000Clearer coding-agents diagram and a wider guide search fieldKTPH001 — the diagram on the coding-agents page shows one short note per box and no longer routes a line through other boxes, and the search field in the guide header is wide enough for its German placeholder.

KTPH000Flow diagrams keep loops a model drew in the wrong shapeKTPH001 — when a model drew a loop's condition as a plain action with two exits, the repair cut the exit after the loop and the whole diagram was replaced by the local fallback. Such a loop head is now turned into the loop decision.

KTPH002Flow diagrams from Nemotron and gpt-oss are no longer thrown awayKTPH003 — a model that writes all branches of a decision in one chain through KTPH004StopKTPH005 (KTPH000), as Nvidia Nemotron does, now gets that chain read as the decision's next outcome instead of the diagram being rejected, and repeated lines no longer make a complete diagram look hollowed out. Rounded nodes such as KTPH001 are read as actions. When a diagram is still rejected — for example because a local model such as gpt-oss derailed into garbled output — korTTY asks once more, naming the reason, before it uses the local fallback.

KTPH000Snippet Manager: more columns, resizable and rememberedKTPH001 — the snippet table shows KTPH002LinesKTPH003 and KTPH004Last modifiedKTPH005, every column (including KTPH006UsedKTPH007, which was too narrow to read, and KTPH008TagsKTPH009) can be resized, and korTTY remembers the widths. KTPH010ExportKTPH011 now proposes plain text script files first. See KTPH012SnippetsKTPH013.

KTPH001Import single text files as snippetsKTPH002 — KTPH003ImportKTPH004 accepts plain text files such as KTPH000, several at once; each becomes a snippet named after the file, with the language taken from the file extension. Binary files are skipped. See KTPH005Importing text filesKTPH006.

KTPH000Import and export snippet variablesKTPH001 — the Variable Manager exports all or the selected variables as JSON, XML or YAML and imports them again, asking whether existing values are overwritten. Its windows are larger, and the add/edit dialog explains both fields. See KTPH002Variable ManagerKTPH003.

KTPH008One workspace for all snippetsKTPH009 — the Snippet Manager shows the library and the snippets you edit side by side: browse in a read-only preview tab, edit in one tab per snippet, find a snippet with quick open (KTPH010KTPH000KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH001KTPH013), hide the library with KTPH014KTPH002KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH003KTPH017, and save or close tabs with KTPH018KTPH004KTPH019+KTPH020KTPH005KTPH021 / KTPH022KTPH006KTPH023+KTPH024KTPH007KTPH025. The open tabs and the window's size and position come back the next time. See KTPH026The Snippet Manager workspaceKTPH027.

KTPH000Unsaved snippets are never lostKTPH001 — every way of closing, including closing a main-window tab, opening a project and quitting, asks about unsaved snippet edits, and an editor's unsaved form is kept as a draft that can be restored after a crash.

KTPH000The Full code analysis lives in the editor and is storedKTPH001 — the analysis is a side panel inside the snippet editor, stored with the snippet the moment it arrives and shown again without a new AI request.
